---
title: "Known Limitations"
description: "Visible boundaries of the current OPALX implementation and documentation."
audience: user
status: experimental
last-reviewed: "2026-07-23"
---

- OPALX is not documented as a drop-in implementation of every historical
  OPAL flavor. OPAL-CYCL and OPAL-MAP material is not part of this manual.
- Registered but regression-untested interfaces are identified as
  source-supported; that label does not claim regression coverage.
- Some physics chapters document recently implemented models whose interface
  may still change; these pages are marked `experimental`.
- Backend support must be checked for each new algorithm; successful serial
  execution does not establish GPU support.
- Hard-edge fields and active elements shorter than a few integration steps can
  create numerical splitting. Always check time-step convergence.
- The experimental [COF command](../user-guide/tracking.qmd#opalx-cof-command)
  solves static, fixed-energy, four-dimensional ring closure. It does not provide
  RF/6D closure, space-charge matching, or automatic integer-tune and plane
  assignment. A converged orbit does not establish stability.
- [COF-to-TRACK handover](../user-guide/tracking.qmd#opalx-initial-orbit)
  requires a fresh generated beam with completed emission. TRACK closure needs
  its own timestep study because its integration and return plane can differ
  from COF's. Explicit `TURNS` currently excludes space charge and RF.

These limitations are documentation status, not a substitute for the issue
tracker. Report unexpected implemented behavior with a reproducible case.
